build: freezer-cartridge backup SENTINEL+ (one packed file) on a disk named P00 IMPORTS, not the original release; its RAM at $FF40-$FFFF (the vectors) comes back as $FF, so it is restarted at the game entry $3F00

exclude: landscape tile data, 32 by 32, generated for each landscape
the play view: five character sets the game draws into, one per 40-line band
bitmap drawn by the game: the title screens show it, and play draws the view into it
title screen colour matrix, written by the game ($8685)
missing in this copy: the freezer backup restored the emulator fill pattern here (orientation.md)
vectors and the BBC-style entry points, written by $8900 at start; $FF in this copy

comments.text: 6510 port direction register, not a game variable. $8903 stores $2F here at start-up and no other traced instruction writes it. The BBC original kept the number of the enemy being processed at this address; the C64 build moved that byte to $90, and the reset loop at $115D starts clearing zero page at $02 so both port registers are left alone.

6510 port data register, i.e. the memory map. $8907 stores $35 at start-up (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000-$DFFF) and no other traced instruction writes it. The BBC original kept the current object number here; on the C64 that byte lives at $91.

Shared byte. In the gaze-versus-tile test at $1CDD it is the position (0-255) along the tile edge where the gaze point lies, stored at $1DBD and used as a multiplier at $1DD2 to interpolate the edge height. In the tile-shape code it is the page of the x-coordinate list an edge is traced into: $2E0D sets $AD, $2E24 bumps it to $AE, and $2F39/$30EA patch it into the store operands at $2F61 and $3121.

Tile column of the viewer in the rotated frame used for drawing (axes turned to match the view direction), written four ways at $268D-$26BF, compared at $2772-$2799 and $2965/$2980 while rows are drawn. The C64-only precompute at $3700 reuses it for the viewer's plain column, loaded from obj_x at $3705 and subtracted at $3720.

Screen y of the lowest point of the polygon being filled (y grows up the screen). Written by the tile-shape code at $2DFC/$2EAC/$2EFA and used as the fill's lower bound in $22AA at $22B3, $230C and $2313.

Offset into the per-corner drawing tables ($0A80, $0AE0, $0BA0, $A800) for the tile being handled: set at $2462, $26D4 and many points in $2625-$27B0, and ORed into the index at $25B2, $284A, $2A17, $2D6E and the C64-only $37F7.

Shared byte. As a tile height: the height limit in $1238 (raised by one after every 256 misses until it reaches 12), the altitude being scanned in $14FB/$159D/$15CC (e.g. $15A4 compare, $1617 store). As a polygon bound: the screen y of the polygon's highest point, set by the tile-shape code ($2DF4, $2F15) and read by the fill at $22B0/$22C2/$2308.
High byte of the smallest yaw angle that still lands inside the current screen buffer. Set by the buffer set-up routines ($2999, $29CA) and checked at $293F and in the C64-only tile loop at $388F.

Direction of the most recent pan: 0 right, 1 left, 2 up, 3 down. Copied from $09 at $3647 when a pan starts (cleared at $3596); read by the pan routine $10B7 to pick the step from $9925, by the C64 scroller $96A6 to pick the scroll direction, and at $1FE0/$207C.

Pan direction currently being requested, same values as $08, bit 7 set for none. $119F sets $80 then stores the sideways or vertical key-logger entry ($120B); the C64 sights code at $997A/$998E/$99B6/$99D0 stores a direction when the sights are pushed past the edge of the view. Read at $12CA, $3645 and $995B.
High byte of the x difference between two polygon points, stored at $3017 in the edge tracer and used at $303E as the sign for $1007 (make positive).

Object number (0-63) of the robot the player is in: written when the player is placed ($1455), on transfer ($1B6C) and hyperspace ($21A5); read all over the enemy, drain and visibility code (e.g. $16E1, $1938, $2481) and by the C64 sights code at $9994 to fetch the player's pitch.

Multi-purpose byte: row counter in the highest-tile search ($15E4-$162B); vertical tolerance when testing a gaze against a tile surface ($1CFF, $1E2E sets $10, compared $1D1E); low byte of the pointer ($0C/$0D) into the secret-code stash on page $3F, built at $254F-$2555 from the stash offset at $0C55 plus 41 and stepped down at $2567; y delta low byte in the tile-edge tracer ($2E18-$3173).

Multi-purpose byte: column counter in the highest-tile search ($15F2-$1625); high byte of the stash pointer at $0C, always $3F ($2559-$255D: 3 + $3C), so the C64 keeps its stash on the page of the start-up code at $3F00; the signed, scaled x step of an edge in the tile-edge tracer ($2F29-$3177).
Holds X (a polygon point number) across the edge tracer: stored at $3002 and restored at $309A to index the pitch tables at $0A80/$0AE0.

Shared byte. In the enemy code ($17AE, $17C8, $17CD) a flag for an enemy that sees the player's robot but not the tile it stands on. In the landscape drawing loop it saves Y across calls ($2847/$2957), and the C64-only loop at $37F4/$38A6 uses it the same way.

Which screen buffer the drawing code is filling (row or column buffer, left or right part). Set by $2993/$29F6 and $1FED/$2033, flipped at $298D, read by the fill ($22CA) and the polygon drawer ($2AA9, $2AB7).
High byte of the offset that turns a yaw measured from the buffer's centre into one measured from its left edge; set by $29A3/$29ED and added at $2DA7/$2DDD in the tile-shape code.
High byte of the largest yaw angle that still lands inside the current screen buffer; set by $299E/$29D6, checked at $2951 and in the C64-only tile loop at $38A0.
Scratch for the C64 dissolve routine $86A5: the random row pick at $8712-$871B, then the masked source pixels at $877F that are ORed into the screen byte at $8786.

Result of an enemy's line-of-sight check on its target: bit 7 when the target's tile can be seen, bit 6 when only the robot itself can. Built in the enemy code ($17DC, $1891), shifted at $18FC, read at $1719-$183F, $19DE and $1AE6.

General loop counter used by many routines: star batches in $1090 (3 passes), placement attempts in $1238 (256 per height), row loops in the fill $2211 ($2243/$2272), smoothing passes $2B87, the four-step bit loop of the 3D digit printer at $3244/$325D, the screen decay at $8805, the icon loop at $9513 and the C64 object redraw at $206A/$2081.
Low byte of the y (pitch) of the end point of the polygon edge being traced ($2E77-$30B3).
Number of edges in the polygon being drawn (set $2D8E, $8593, compared $2E8F) or, in the visibility tracer, the number of steps along the ray ($24F5, halved at $253E, used at $2576).
Multi-purpose: tile column in the highest-tile block search ($15D5/$15F4) and in the row visibility trace ($24EB-$25BC); low byte of an edge's start x in the edge tracer ($2E7C-$3165).

Colour pair of the polygon being drawn (fill and edge colours), set by the tile and object drawers ($2A60, $2A94, $2AA1, $8589) and read by the fill at $22E0/$22EB; also a row number in the visibility trace ($24FC).

Multi-purpose: tile row in the highest-tile search ($15DB/$15E6) and visibility trace ($2471-$24E2); the screen line being filled ($230A-$239E); low byte of an edge's start y in the edge tracer ($2E6D-$30E8).

Offset into the drawing tables for the quadrant holding the right-hand edge of the 90-degree view: $266D-$2670 look it up in the four-byte table at $27D3 from the top two bits of the arc yaw; added at $2A1A.

Shared byte: the yaw of the right edge of the view arc (viewer yaw + $20, stored $265C, tested $2684/$28A3 and at $37FB in the C64 loop), or the action code for the landscape data pass run by $2B22/$2BBC (bit tests at $2BC5, $2BDB, $2C65).

Tile row of the viewer in the rotated drawing frame, companion of $03: written at $2692-$26C7, compared $26F5, subtracted at $2879. The C64-only precompute reuses it for the viewer's plain row, loaded from obj_z at $370A and subtracted at $3736.

Counter reused by unrelated loops: trees still to plant ($1497/$14A6), gaze checks in the anti-tamper routine at $1887 ($18D6/$1912), extra columns for the fill ($2222/$2276), horizontal edges in the tile-shape code ($2DF8-$2EDB) and dots in the C64 screen decay ($8801/$8811).

Low byte of a yaw offset applied while redrawing a single object so that its left edge sits at the buffer's left edge; set at $1FD0/$2003, subtracted at $2894, $8418 and in the C64 tile loop at $3854.
High byte of the yaw of the screen's left edge reduced to one quadrant; stored at $2682, subtracted at $289B.

Index of the tile corner or object point being written to the drawing tables ($0A80/$0AE0/$0BA0/$A800): set at $284C and $8479, stepped at $8527; the C64-only precompute makes it (column*8 AND $E0) OR row at $3755 and uses it at $37C7; the C64 tile loop makes it Y OR $05 at $37F9 and uses it at $384F.
Two-byte pointer ($22/$23) to the screen or buffer byte being plotted: stars at $9406-$9451, the C64 random-dot plot at $9498/$94BC, and the scanner static at $1665/$167C (high byte fixed at $70).
High byte of the plot pointer at $22: star row page at $9413/$9433 (wrapped into the view buffer at $9422-$9431), $94A1 in the dot plotter, $1669 (= $70) for the scanner.

Tile column 0-31 of the square being worked on; one of the most used variables. Set by callers before $2BA8 (pointer to the square's byte in $0400-$07FF), stepped in the generator and smoothing loops ($2B03, $2B98), the spawn code ($124D, $1463, $1F16) and the C64 per-square precompute at $3712-$37E3.
Column of the tile being drawn in the landscape row loop ($295F-$2987, $2A15, $2A4D, $2D6C) or the number of columns left to fill in $2211 ($2224/$223F).
Tile row 0-31 of the square being worked on, the partner of $24 (the pointer at $2BA8 is built from both); also the fill's current character row at $2211/$2233/$227F and the digit row at $322B.
Bit mask with as many leading zeroes as the count it was made from: set by $15BE (tiles at one height) and $24B1, used to limit a random pick at $151E and $24CB.
Low byte of the smallest yaw inside the current screen buffer (pair of $07); set $29B6/$29CF, checked $2948 and $3898.
Low byte of the buffer's yaw-origin offset (pair of $11); set $29B8/$29F2, added $2DA0/$2DD6.
Random byte used to pick a star's pixel in the star plotter $93F5: stored at $940B from $93F0, rotated at $9435 to choose one of four pixels. $2B after it is not referenced.

Lowest byte of the x part of a 3D vector (e.g. eye to sights, written $1C9A, added $1CC4, $250C-$2532), and in the fill a flag that the polygon ran past the buffer's right edge ($22AC, $2333, $233C, read $2AB9).
Lowest byte of the y part of a 3D vector ($1C67, $2536, $2595), and in the fill the flag that the polygon ran past the left edge ($22AE, $232D, $234F).
Lowest byte of the z part of a 3D vector; shifted at $253A in the visibility tracer.
Low byte of the x part of a 3D vector: set $1C96, $2512; added $1CC8, $257D; shifted $2534.
Low byte of the y part of a 3D vector ($1C65, $1D2E, $2538, $259B), or in the tile-shape code the smallest x of the horizontal edges found ($2DFE-$2ED9).
Low byte of the z part of a 3D vector ($253C, $2588), or in the tile-shape code the largest x of the horizontal edges ($2DF6-$2ED3).
Leftmost tile of the row being drawn ($26D0-$2721, $27D7-$2829), or the low byte of cos(pitch) when turning angles into a vector ($1C5E, read $1C81).
Rightmost tile of the row being drawn ($26E8-$274F, $27FC-$281A), or the high byte of cos(pitch) in the vector code ($1C5C, $1C85).
Lowest byte of a 24-bit x coordinate ($1CC1/$1CC6, $1ECE), or the tile shape number used as a colour-table offset in the two-face tile drawer ($2A8A/$2A99).
Lowest byte of a 24-bit y coordinate ($1ED0, $2592/$2597), or the buffer's left edge in pixels ($29AD/$29E8, used by the fill at $2380/$23A9).
Lowest byte of a 24-bit z coordinate ($1ED2), or the buffer's right edge in pixels ($29B2/$29E3, compared at $23A4).
Middle byte of a 24-bit x coordinate ($1CCE/$1CD0, $1ED6, $257A/$257F), or the leftmost visible tile of the row being drawn ($26E6-$2786, $295D/$297C).
Middle byte of a 24-bit y coordinate ($1D11, $1E6D, $1EDD, $2599/$259D), or the rightmost visible tile of the row ($26EA-$278B, $2961/$2973).
Middle byte of a 24-bit z coordinate ($1DA6, $1ED8, $2585/$258A), or the low byte of an edge's end x in the edge tracer ($2E81-$30C0).
High byte of a 24-bit x coordinate (tile column plus fraction: $1CD2-$1CEB, $1EE2, $2510; read at $1BC7 by the transfer code), or the low byte of an edge's x step ($3047, $3077).
High byte of a 24-bit y (height) coordinate ($1D16, $1D72, $1EE7, $259F/$25A3), or the polygon kind in bits 6-7 for the drawer (set $2A64, $2A8F, $8542; tested $2D70).

High byte of a 24-bit z coordinate ($1CF3, $1EEC, read by the transfer code at $1BCB), or the low byte of the pointer ($3C/$3D) to the list of point numbers of the polygon being drawn: $0C40 for a tile face (set at $2650/$2654), the object's polygon data from $A2E0/$A420 in the object drawer ($8598/$85B8); read through at $2D99-$2E0A.
Low byte of a vector's yaw ($1C21, $18CE, read $1C69), or the high byte of the polygon point-list pointer at $3C ($0C for tile faces at $2654, from $A420 for objects at $859D/$85BC).
High byte of a vector's yaw ($1C2B, $18D2, read $1C6D), or the high byte of an edge's start y in the edge tracer ($2E68-$3188, $314E, $31A5).
Low byte of a vector's pitch ($1C46, $18EB), or the high byte of an edge's end y in the edge tracer ($2E72-$30A4).

High byte of a vector's pitch ($1C52, $18F1), or the shift count used to squeeze an edge's x and y deltas into single bytes in the edge tracer (cleared at $3006, rotated at $302B, read $305D, counted down $3086).
High byte of the start x of the polygon edge being traced ($2E85-$319A); read at $31AF by the code that patches the edge-storing instructions.
High byte of the end x of the polygon edge being traced ($2E87-$30C6).
High byte of the signed, scaled x step of the edge being traced: stored at $3043, subtracted at $307F. $44 after it is not referenced.
Number of the first corner used when a tile's shape is split into faces: stored by $2A46/$2A79, read at $2D49 by the tile-shape code. $46-$49 after it are not referenced.
Index of the polygon side being processed in the tile-shape code: stored $2E04, read $2E8C.
Quadrant number opposite to the one holding the right edge of the view arc; stored at $267B, read by the tile drawers at $2A42 and $2A81.

Type of the object whose screen angles are being computed: set from the type table at $0A40 by $8406, indexes the shape data at $8475/$854B/$856F; also read at $18D8 in the anti-tamper routine at $1887. $4D after it is not referenced.
Loop counter over an object's points ($8483-$8529, while angles are computed) or over its faces ($8579, $85A2, while drawing).
End value for the loop counter at $4E: the object's last point ($847E, compared $852B) or last face ($8574, compared $85A5).
Low byte of a difference between two pitch angles: made at $9363 (then divided by 16 with the RORs at $936C-$9375), read at $2937 and $8520.
Largest pitch that fits the current screen buffer: the C64 sets it from the table at $994B ($F0 for both buffers) at $9943; compared at $2EA8-$2F10 when a tile's points are clipped.
Smallest pitch that fits the current screen buffer: $9948 loads it from $994D ($B0 for the row buffer, $30 for the column buffer); compared at $2EA4-$2F04.
Pass counter for objects drawn in more than one pass by the object drawer: set $8546/$856D, read $857E, counted down $85A9.
Screen byte that was behind the right edge of the polygon line being filled; saved at $2394, reused at $2359.

Written but never read in this image: $3594 stores 0 and $35CE stores $19 when a landscape starts. In the BBC original the drawing code tested it to draw either to the screen or into the buffer; no traced C64 instruction reads it (searched named and indexed operands), though the missing code at $B000-$B5FF could.
Screen x of the right end of the polygon line being filled ($233A, $2390, compared $23B1, $23D1).
Rows left to fill in the screen-fill routine $2211 (set $2213 from Y, counted down $2281).
Pixel byte holding four pixels of the polygon's fill colour, made at $2306 and stored at $23D7.
Low byte of the difference between the viewer's yaw and the yaw of the object being measured (made $842F/$844A in $8401, read $8485).
High byte of the yaw difference at $59 ($8436/$8446, read $8489 and $8555). $5B after it is not referenced.
Low byte of the second (opposite) side given to the hypotenuse routines: stored $929B/$92AE in $9287, read $938D in $937F.
High byte of the opposite side ($9297/$92AA, read $9391).

Pointer ($5E/$5F) to a square's byte in the landscape grid at $0400-$07FF, always used with Y as ($5E),Y. The low byte stays 0 (cleared by the reset at $115D); $2BA8 puts the page in $5F and the row/column index in Y. Read and written through it everywhere tiles are tested or changed ($1257, $1F7C, $2B12, $377C).
Page of the landscape square pointer at $5E: 4 + (column AND 3), set by $2BB9 and by the C64-only loops at $375F/$383D; each page holds 256 squares.

In the sine/cosine routine $0E75 the index (0 or 1) of the value computed second ($0E88-$0F01). In the gaze code the control bits for $1DF9: bit 7 = let a boulder or the Sentinel's tower on the square count towards its height, bit 6 = report where the gaze meets it ($1CFD, $1D22, $1D4A, $1E42, $1EA2); cleared at $25C8.
Width in pixels of the current screen buffer: set $29A8/$29DC, read by the fill at $2337/$2384.

Source pointer ($62/$63) for the C64's copying of the drawn view: the dissolve at $86A5 reads buffer pixels through it ($872A, $877A); the column and block copiers at $9730-$98DB step it by $140 per row.
High byte of the copy source pointer at $62: set $8733, $9745, $98DB; incremented in the unrolled copy loops at $984C and $9880.

Destination pointer ($64/$65) into the character-set memory the play screen shows, built from the row tables $3A00/$3A20 plus column*8 ($875E, $9763, $97B3) and written through by the copiers at $9812-$98AF and the dissolve at $8788.
High byte of the copy destination at $64 ($8767, $976A, $97BA); the column copier adds and removes the extra page offset from $3A40 around its second copy ($9775-$9782).
Action code for the landscape smoothing pass ($2B83, ORed at $2BBC) or the arc quadrant times 4 used when counting a sloping tile's faces ($2675, subtracted $2A6B).

Sign flags for the maths routines: $0F70 stores the angle so that bit 7 gives the sign of the sine and bit 6 that of the cosine (tested $0F8C, $84A2); $0F9E flips bit 7 for each negative factor and $1005 applies it to the product; set by $1C7F.
Low byte of the second factor of the 16x16 multiply at $0F9E, sign-magnitude with the sign in bit 0 ($0FB5); set by $1C8C.
High byte of the second factor of the 16x16 multiply ($0FD7, $0FED); set by $1C91.
Low byte of the first (two's complement) factor of the 16x16 multiply; negated in place at $0FA5-$0FA7, read $0FE9; set by $1C83.
High byte of the first factor of the 16x16 multiply; its sign is tested at $0F9E, negated $0FAB-$0FAD, read $0FC1; set by $1C87.

Flag telling the tile-shape code whether the polygon's pixel x coordinates need two bytes (bit 6); set $2D95/$2DCB, tested $2E3B. $6D after it is not referenced on the C64 (the BBC's scroll routine used it).

Object number of whoever is looking: the player for the view and pans ($10B9, $2625), an enemy while it scans for targets ($16E3, $1773), the object on the title or game-over picture ($13F5, $8852); also a loop counter while enemies are placed ($1500-$156D). The C64-only precompute at $3700 reads it.
Number of the object whose screen angles $8401 works out (stored $8401, read $8428 and $85C1).

Scratch byte. Mostly the low byte of a store pointer ($70/$71) in the fill's unrolled loops at $2238-$2456; a work byte in $245B/$25C6-$2617; and in the C64 screen-matrix reset $9AAC the pointer that walks $7C00 in 240-byte steps.
Scratch byte, the high half of the pointer at $70 in the fill (set $223D/$234B/$23CD, stepped $227A) and in the matrix reset $9AB6-$9ACD; also read as a value in $245B-$25C4.
Scratch byte used by the fill ($22AA) and the visibility code ($24E2-$25C4); in the C64 visibility loop it is the low byte of a pointer compared through at $25A5.
Scratch byte: fill, visibility and gaze code ($1CDD, $22AA, $24E2-$25C4, $2C7C); the high byte of the pointer at $72 in the C64 visibility loop (set from $3C + $40 at $2548, updated $258C-$2590).

Main scratch byte and the low half of most 16-bit results: (A $74) is the product of $0D03/$0F4A/$0F9E, the dividend of $0D4A, the angle given to $0E75/$0F3E/$0F70, the value $1007/$1009 negate. Used by about forty routines.

Second scratch byte: the 8-bit factor of $0D03 and $0F4A, the high byte returned by $0F3E/$0F4A and $1009, a counter in $8643 (colours left to set, $864A/$8697) and a work byte in many other routines.
Scratch byte: high byte of the divisor for the arctangent at $0D4A (compared $0D4F-$0DE2), high byte of the 16-bit factor of $0F4A, and a work byte in the edge tracer and elsewhere.
Scratch byte: low byte of the arctangent divisor ($0D57, $0D5F), holds the partial product in $0F4A ($0F4D/$0F56) and $0F9E ($0FCA-$0FE3).
Scratch byte: collects two extra quotient bits for interpolation in $0D4A ($0DF1/$0DF8, tested $0E2C-$0E5F), the top byte of the 16x16 product ($0FDC-$1003) and a work byte in the gaze code.
Fractional part of the height of a boulder or the Sentinel's tower found under the gaze: cleared $1D03, set by $1DF9, read $1D0E-$1D2E.
Low byte of the first (adjacent) side given to the hypotenuse routines ($9287, $937F).
High byte of the adjacent side ($9287, $937F).
Low byte of the hypotenuse (horizontal distance) worked out by $937F; read by $8401 and $933D, and by the C64 precompute at $37B8, which feeds it back as a side for the pitch angle.
High byte of the hypotenuse from $937F; read by $8401, $8533, $933D and the C64 precompute at $37BC.
Tangent (times 256) found by the arctangent at $0D4A and used as the table index there ($0E05 sets $FF, $0E20 stores it); also set at $9280 and read at $9382.
Whether the tile being drawn lies on, partly on or off the screen, or whether the polygon being traced has any visible pixels (non-zero = skip it): $2D6C-$2EE4, $31A4, and the C64 tile loop at $38A8.
Low byte of an x difference between two points: made by $85C4 and by the C64 precompute ($3719-$37B0), used by the hypotenuse and angle routines ($9287, $933D) and $283D, $1887, $209B.
Low byte of a y (height) difference, made by $85F5 and read by $8401 and $1887.
Low byte of a z difference (made by $85C4, the C64 precompute $371B/$37BA), used with $80 by $9287 and $933D.
Absolute value of the high byte of the x difference ($85C4, $3731/$37B6), compared at $9289.
High byte of the y difference, made at $8604 by $85F5 and read by $8401.
Absolute value of the high byte of the z difference ($85C4, $3747/$37BE), compared at $9287.
Signed high byte of the x difference ($85C4, $3722/$37A7), or the high byte of the x part of a ray in the visibility tracer ($24E2-$2516).
High byte of the y part of a ray in the visibility tracer; read at $25A1 by the C64 version of that loop.
Signed high byte of the z difference ($85C4, $3738/$37C2), or the high byte of the z part of a ray in the visibility tracer. $89 after it is not referenced.

Low byte of the 16-bit angle returned by the arctangent $0D4A and the hypotenuse-angle routine $9287; read by $8401, $8475, $933D, $1887, $209B and the C64 precompute, which stores it per square at $3771 and rescales it at $37CD-$37DF.
High byte of that angle (a full turn is 256 in this byte): set by $0D4A/$9287, stored per square by the C64 precompute at $3775/$37C9. $8C after it is not referenced.
High byte of a difference between two pitch angles (made in $933D, read $283D and $8475).
Size of the sine of an angle, 8 bits, from the table at $AC80 via $0F70 (stored $0F92/$0F9B); signs in bits 7/6 of $67. Read by $8475.
Size of the cosine of the same angle, 8 bits, from $AC80 via $0F70 (stored $0F94/$0F99); read by $8475.

Number (0-7) of the enemy being handled in this turn of the main loop: read by the tactics code at $16B9-$1A5D to index the per-enemy tables at $0C20-$0CBF, and stepped once per turn: $16D9 counts it down and $16DD-$16DF wrap it from -1 back to 7. The BBC original kept this at $00, which is the 6510's own register on the C64.

Number of the object being processed by the object routines: set at $187B, $1B06, $1BA1, $212C; read at $1A7D, $2163, $21A3 and $209B; the game-over code sets it to 1 at $87E5-$87E7. The BBC original kept this at $01, the 6510's port register on the C64.

Low byte of column*8 (the byte offset of a character column within a row of the view's character data), made at $8745, $9750 and $97A2 and added to the row base from $3A00 to form the destination pointer at $64.
High byte of column*8 (the carry, for columns 32-39): $874A, $9755, $97A7; added with the row base high byte from $3A20.

Screen column (0-39) where the view's left edge currently starts: the C64 scrolls sideways by moving this origin round a 40-column ring instead of copying the whole view. Reset to 0 by $1336 and $98B8, stepped by the pan scroller at $96AC-$96BE (wraps 0/39), read at $2039 and $9712.

Screen row (0-24) where the view's top currently starts, the vertical partner of $94: reset by $1345/$98BA, stepped by $96F2-$9704 (wraps 0/24), used by the interrupt set-up at $9597 to place the raster splits and by the dot plotter at $9477.

Screen column where the next strip of new picture is copied: origin plus the table at $990D for the pan direction, modulo 40 ($96C0-$96CA); also set at $2041/$207A for an object redraw and to 0 at $98B4. Used as column*8 by the copiers at $974B-$97F4 and by the dissolve at $8738.

Screen row where the next strip goes, modulo 25 ($96CE, $9706-$9710), set at $2045 and $98B6, counted up by the full-screen copy at $98E0; indexes the row tables $3A00/$3A20/$3A40 ($9757, $97A9, $874F).
Rows left in the column copy at $9730: set to 24 ($9759-$975B), counted down at $9798.

Second destination pointer ($99/$9A). For screen rows where the table at $3A40 gives a non-zero page offset, the copiers and the dissolve write every byte twice, to ($64) and to this pointer ($8788/$878A, $9814/$9816); $99 is a copy of $64's low byte ($8760, $97E9, $97FF).
High byte of the second destination: the high byte at $65 plus the page offset from $3A40 for that row ($876D, $97E5, $980B).

Horizontal position of the sights in view pixels, the value the C64 turns into sprite 0's x (x*2+14, with bit 8 in $D010) at $99EE-$9A0A. A copy of $0CC6, made at $1359, $96ED and by the sights movers $9972/$9986.
Vertical position of the sights, turned into sprite 0's y as $F9 minus it at $99E1-$99E6. A copy of $0CC7 made at $1360, $9728, $99A8, $99C2, $99D9.
Column (0 to buffer width-1) of the byte the dissolve at $86A5 copies next; a random walk: the random byte plus the old value, masked and wrapped ($86F5-$8703).
Character row (0-23) of the byte the dissolve copies next: 3/4 of a random 0-31 ($8712-$871B).
Pixel line pair (0-3) within the character for the dissolve; lines $9F and $9F+4 are copied ($8705-$870D, used $8723 and $8743). $A0 after it is not referenced.

Second pointer ($A1/$A2) of the dot plotter at $945F: for rows with a non-zero page offset at $3A40 each dot is written to ($22) and again here ($94BC/$94BE); the low byte is copied from $22 at $949A.
High byte of the dot plotter's second pointer: $23 plus the page offset from $3A40 ($94A3-$94A7).
Middle byte of the dissolve's 24-bit random number (low byte at $87B0, high byte at $A4), multiplied by 5 on each step at $86C1-$86ED.
High byte of the dissolve's random number; after each step it gives the column offset ($86EF-$86FB).
Scratch for the dissolve's random step: low byte of the number times 4 ($86C4-$86DE).
Scratch: middle byte of the random number times 4 ($86C8-$86E5).
Scratch: high byte of the random number times 4 ($86CC-$86EB).

Pointer ($A8/$A9, low byte always 0) to the C64's table of yaw angles (low bytes) from the viewer (normally the player) to every square, at $BC00-$BFFF, laid out like the landscape grid. Written through at $3773 by the precompute at $3700, read at $3851 by the drawing loop.
Page of the yaw-low table: $BC + (column AND 3), set at $3763 and $3841; the three other table pages at $AB, $AD, $AF are this plus 4, 8 and 12.
Pointer ($AA/$AB, low byte 0) to the C64's table of yaw angle high bytes per square at $C000-$C3FF ($3777 writes, $3859 reads).
Page of the yaw-high table, $C0-$C3 ($3767, $3845).

Pointer ($AC/$AD, low byte 0) to the table of pitch angles per square, low bytes, at $C400-$C7FF; the precompute stores the 16-bit angle divided by 16 ($37C9-$37DF), low byte through this pointer at $37E1; read at $3860.
Page of the pitch-low table, $C4-$C7 ($376B, $3849).
Pointer ($AE/$AF, low byte 0) to the table of pitch angle high bytes per square at $C800-$CBFF, sign-extended ($37DD writes, $3868 reads).
Page of the pitch-high table, $C8-$CB ($376F, $384D).
Low byte of the viewer's pitch rescaled to the precomputed tables' units (pitch*16 + 2, 16-bit), made by the C64 insert at $2627-$2644 at the start of each view; subtracted at $3863.
High byte of the rescaled viewer pitch, sign-extended ($2640); subtracted at $386A.
Viewer's yaw minus 10, made at $2646-$264C; subtracted from each square's precomputed yaw at $385B, so the drawing loop gets yaws relative to the view.

$B3-$EF: no traced instruction names these bytes (the indexed zero-page accesses, such as $1DBF and $2507, use small indexes). They still hold the KERNAL's own work values from before the game took over (for example the screen line bytes $84-$87 at $D9-$EF) and are identical in work/entry.vsf and work/play-l0000.vsf. Whether the missing $B000-$B5FF code uses them is unknown.

Pointer ($F0/$F1) to a glyph of the BBC Micro font at $8000 + 8 * character: set by the C64 text printer at $8BDC-$8BEC and by the character-definition call (OSWORD 10 emulation) at $8D92-$8DA2; read through at $8C46/$8C68/$8DAC.
High byte of the glyph pointer: $80 + character/32 ($8BEC, $8DA2).

Two uses in the C64's stand-in for the BBC system calls: the pointer ($F2/$F3) to the colour-matrix cell at $CC00 + cell that the text printer writes ($8C15/$8C21), and the parameter block address passed in X/Y to the OSWORD 10 emulation ($8D8C/$8D8A), whose 8 glyph bytes are copied there ($8DAE).
High byte of the pointer at $F2 ($8C21 = $CC + row page; $8D8A from Y).

Pointer ($F4/$F5) to the bitmap byte at $E000 + 8 * cell that the C64 text printer draws into ($8C3A/$8C35); written through with colour masks at $8CC1/$8CDE. Each 8-pixel row of a BBC glyph becomes two multicolour bytes: the high nibble goes into one cell, then $8C53-$8C5E move the pointer 8 bytes on to the next cell for the low nibble.
High byte of the text printer's bitmap pointer: $E0 + cell*8 / 256 ($8C35, $8C5A-$8C5E).
Pointer ($F6/$F7) to the sound parameter block given in X/Y to the C64's OSWORD 7 emulation (make a sound): set $8DB4, read through at $8DBA-$8E7A to program the SID.
High byte of the sound parameter block pointer ($8DB6).
$F8-$FF: not named by any traced instruction, directly or through an index, and unchanged between the hand-over and play snapshots.

Flags of the 64 object slots, $0100-$013F: bit 7 set = slot free; bit 6 set = the object stands on another, whose number is in bits 0-5. $118B sets all to $80; searched for a free slot at $2122; the reset loop at $116B clears $0100-$01BF. Game data kept in the stack page; the stack itself works down from $01FF.

Pitch (up/down angle) of each of the 64 objects, $0140-$017F: $F5 when placed ($1F7E); the player's changes by 4 per up/down pan ($10FF-$1145); read by the view set-up $262B, the sights code $9996 and $933D, $1C4C.
obj_pitch entries 2-15: object 2 is the viewer of the title and game-over pictures, whose pitch $8839 sets from $8872+Y.
obj_pitch entries 16-63: $13CB sets object 16's, the viewer of the title and preview views.

Work area $0180-$01BF shared by the landscape drawing: the visibility of the tile corners of two rows (from $0180 and $01A0) while rows are traced ($245B-$24BC), and the square data of the tiles in view ($283D, $29C7, $2A12, the C64 loop at $3871).
row_visibility+1: $24B6 ORs in the neighbouring corner of the first row (ORA $0181,X).
Second half of the corner-visibility area, $01A0-$01BF (the other row); read at $24B9.
$01A0 entry plus one: $24BC ORs in the neighbouring corner of the second row.

256 pseudo-random bytes, $0200-$02FF, made once at start-up: $3F96-$3FAF fill the seed register with ones, run it 256 times and store the next 256 results here. Only reader: the scanner static at $1670, whose operand low byte is stepped down by $166D (self-modifying), so it walks backwards through the table.

$0300-$03FF, the BASIC and KERNAL vector page, left as the system had it ($0314/$0315 still hold $EA31, the KERNAL's interrupt entry) and not used by the game: the KERNAL is banked out ($01 = $35) and the game sets its own vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF ($8900). No traced instruction reaches this page (named, indexed or indirect) and it is identical in work/entry.vsf and work/play-l0000.vsf. $035C-$03FB hold spaces left by the loading environment.

Tile column (x, 0-31) of each of the 64 objects, $0900-$093F, indexed by object number: set when an object is placed ($1F18), read wherever positions are needed ($1986-$2625, $85C4, the C64 precompute at $3702); cleared by the reset at $1157.
obj_x entry 1: on the title and game-over pictures object 1 is the object shown, and $8830-$8833 give it the viewer's column.
obj_x entries 2-15. Object 2 is the viewer of the title and game-over pictures; $8830 copies its column to object 1.
obj_x entries 16-62: $13D1 puts object 16, the viewer of the title and preview views, in its column.
obj_x entry 63: slot 63 is the object used to draw the blocks of the title's 3D lettering; $2A03-$2A05 put it in the column of the tile being drawn before $8533 draws it.

Height of each object, whole units, $0940-$097F (the fraction is in $0A00): written only at $1F76 when an object is placed (on the ground or on top of another), read by the drawing, gaze and delta code ($1DF9, $245B, $283D, $85F5, the C64 precompute at $378C/$37A4).
obj_y_hi entry 1: $8826-$882D put the displayed object at the viewer's height plus the offset at $8875+Y.
obj_y_hi entries 2-15; object 2's height is read at $8826 for the picture layout.
obj_y_hi entries 16-62: $13C5 sets the height of object 16, the title and preview viewer.
obj_y_hi entry 63: $3291 sets the 3D-lettering block object's height to 2 when the title is drawn.
Tile row (z, 0-31) of each object, $0980-$09BF: set with obj_x when an object is placed ($1F1D), read with it everywhere positions are compared (the C64 precompute reads the viewer's at $3707).
obj_z entry 1: $8820-$8823 put the displayed object at the viewer's row plus the offset at $8855+Y.
obj_z entries 2-15: object 2's row, read at $8820.
obj_z entries 16-62: $13D7 sets the row of object 16, the title and preview viewer.
obj_z entry 63: $2A08-$2A0A put the 3D-lettering block object in the row of the tile being drawn.

Yaw (compass direction, 256 to a turn) each object faces, $09C0-$09FF: set when placed, turned by pans ($10BF-$10FB), U-turns ($1B34-$1B39) and the enemies' turning; read by the view set-up ($2646, $2656) and the object code. The reset loop clears only up to $09EF.
obj_yaw entry 1: the displayed object's direction on the picture, from $8878+Y ($884D).
obj_yaw entries 2-15: $883F sets the picture viewer's direction from $887B+Y.
obj_yaw entries 16-62: $13DD sets the direction of object 16, the title and preview viewer.
obj_yaw entry 63: $3285-$3287 turn the 3D-lettering block object to $80 (facing the other way).
Fraction of each object's height (1/256 units), $0A00-$0A3F, the low byte to obj_y_hi at $0940; set by placing and stacking, read by $1DF9, $283D and $85F5 and by the C64 precompute ($379D).
obj_y_lo entry 1: cleared for the displayed object at $8847.
obj_y_lo entries 2-62: $8844 clears the picture viewer's fraction.
obj_y_lo entry 63: $E0 for the 3D-lettering block object ($328C).

Type of each object, $0A40-$0A7F: 0 robot (the player's is made at $1450-$1452), 1 sentry ($1502), 2 tree ($176B, $1A49), 3 boulder, 4 meanie ($19EE), 5 the Sentinel (object 0, $155B), 6 its tower, 7-9 the halves of the title's 3D letter blocks. Written when objects are made ($2131, $1504, $155D) or change type ($176D, $19F0, $1A4B); read all through the enemy and object code ($16BB-$16C4 pick out types 1 and 5, the enemies).
obj_type entries 1-62: $8819 sets the type of object 1, the object shown on the title or game-over picture, from A.
obj_type entry 63: $29FC-$29FE set it from the low nibble of the tile data (7-9 for the lettering blocks, 0 for none).

Low byte of the screen pitch of each point being drawn, $0A80-$0ADF, 96 entries: 0-31 and 32-63 the tile corners of two landscape rows (the half chosen by $05), 64-95 the points of an object. Written by $2939, the C64 tile loop ($3865) and the object point code ($8522); read by the tile-shape code ($2E11-$309C).
draw_pitch_lo from entry 1 on: $27A8-$27AB copy an entry into the next one at the end of a row.
High byte of the screen pitch of each point being drawn, $0AE0-$0B3F, the same 96 entries as $0A80: $851D for object points, $386C in the C64 tile loop; read $2E1D-$30A1.
draw_pitch_hi from entry 1: $27A5 copies an entry into the next one.
draw_pitch_hi entry 32, the first of the second tile row: $27B4-$27B6 store $FF.
draw_pitch_hi entries 33-95: $27B9 stores $FF in the entry after the one at $27B6.
High byte of the screen x of each point being drawn, $0B40-$0B9F, 96 entries matching $0A80; made and read by the tile-shape code ($2D6C-$3017).
draw_x_hi entries 22-85. The instruction that makes this symbol, LDA $0B56,X at $254F, is a disguise: X is $FF there, so it reads $0C55, the stash offset.

Low byte of the screen yaw of each point being drawn, $0BA0-$0BFF, the same 96 entries; the high bytes are at $A800. Written by the row code ($2896) and the C64 tile loop ($3856); read at $2945, $2D9C, $2DD2.
draw_yaw_lo entries 11-74. LDY $0BAB,X at $14AC is a disguised read of $0C55 (X = $AA), not of this table.

Low byte of the 16-bit sine made by $0E75 (stored through $0C00,X with X=0 at $0EC5/$0EEA/$0EF5); bit 0 is the sign, set at $0F20-$0F23 when the sine is negative. Read by the vector code as $0C00,Y at $1C89 and $1C9D. The reset loop at $1174 also starts its $0C00-$0CEF sweep here.
Low byte of the 16-bit cosine made by $0E75 (the X=1 slot of $0C00,X); bit 0 is its sign, set at $0F31-$0F34.
High bytes of the 16-bit sine ($0C02) and cosine ($0C03), stored as $0C02,X by $0E75 at $0EBE/$0EFA and read as $0C02,Y at $1C8E/$1CA2.

Scanner state to show next: 0 off, 4 static, 8 solid. $1635 redraws the scanner on every call while this is non-zero (fresh static each time, and it becomes $0C09) and once more when it drops to 0. Stored from Y by the energy-drain code at $194D; cleared at $359E when a landscape starts.

Next column (0-39) of the top screen row where $9579 puts an energy icon: cleared at $950A, used as the index into the screen matrix at $7C00 ($957A) and stepped at $9583; $9556/$9567 stop the icon loops at columns 29 and 38. On the C64 the icons are characters $F0-$F9 in that row.

Height of the lowest enemy on the landscape, stored at $1598 when enemies are placed and used as the height limit for placing the player ($146F), new trees ($149E) and trees an enemy makes with spare energy ($1A6A).
Most enemies the landscape may have: 1 + (landscape number / 10), at most 8, worked out by $33ED-$3410 from the BCD landscape number; read by $1420-$1431 when the enemies are chosen.
Multiplier for the landscape's heights, which sets how rugged it is: $18 for landscape 0000, otherwise $0E plus a value from $3451 ($2AD7-$2AE6); applied at $2B58.
Scanner state last drawn by $1635: 0 off (sprites 1-3 hidden), 4 static, 8 solid; also copied to $16A0 as the offset into the scanner patterns at $16A1. Written $163F, compared $163A.

The player's energy in units (tree 1, boulder 2, robot 3): set at $1459 when the player is placed, changed by the drain code ($1A0F-$1A17) and by absorbing and creating ($2139-$214A); read by $3464 to print it and by $9510 to draw the icons. The byte after it, $0C0B, is not referenced.
High byte of the angle given to $0E75, kept for the quadrant tests: stored $0E75, bit 6 tested at $0E8C to swap sine and cosine, bits 7 and 6 at $0F19-$0F2A for the signs.
Stack pointer saved at $16B6 when the enemy tactics code starts, so that $1AF9-$1AFD can abandon the tactics from any depth: TXS, then on at $16D6 with the next enemy.
Yaw step used when a meanie turns to look for the player, stored at $1731 and added at $1741.
Bit 7 set: $AA44 prints characters plainly; clear: with the drop shadow. $3339-$333A set it before the input buffer is printed and $3353 clears it afterwards.

Nine-byte parameter block $0C10-$0C18 for the character-definition request (OSWORD 10 through $FFF1, emulated at $8D81): byte 0 is the character code (stored $3205), bytes 1-8 receive its eight rows from the font at $8000. The 3D title-digit printer then shifts the rows out bit by bit ($323A, $3246, $324A; $326A).
Tile column of the Sentinel, stored at $1558 when the enemies are placed; $2189 compares it on hyperspace (to see whether the player is on the Sentinel's square).
Tile row of the Sentinel, stored at $1553; compared at $2191.
Bit 7 set while a pan strip is drawn without the sights ($3657, cleared $365D): the view drawer tests it at $2760 and gives up the strip as soon as the pan key is released.

Object type shown in the title and game-over pictures: $13AB sets it for the title, and during play the enemy code records the type of the enemy acting against the player ($16C6: 1 sentry or 5 Sentinel; $1722: 4 meanie; $1B24: 0). $87DA reads it so that the game-over picture shows the enemy that did it; $13E7 reads it on the title.
Key-logger value of the latest pan key (0 right, 1 left, 2 up, 3 down), stored at $1211 and compared by $1223 with the current keys.
Bit 7 set: redraw objects at once instead of dissolving them in. Set with $0CE4 at $1219, cleared at $12F6, $1F9B, $364E and $87F1; the C64 dissolve at $8797 stops early when it is set.
Bit 7 set when the pan key used for the last pan is still held after the scroll finished: cleared at $128E, set at $129C from $1223; tested at $1B01.

Eight bytes, one per enemy: countdown before the enemy may drain energy again. $1317 counts all 24 bytes of $0C20-$0C37 down (stopping at 1) on every third call, and on the C64 those calls pass through the extra divider at $130C, which lets only about four in five through. The tactics code sets them ($175A-$1869, $1A33) and tests them ($1795, $182E, $193C).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: countdown to the enemy's next turn, counted down with the other timers by $131E; tested $17FB, reloaded $1815.

Eight bytes, one per enemy: countdown to the next time tactics are applied to that enemy, set when enemies are placed ($157D) and by the tactics code ($16EF-$1870). The eight bytes after it, $0C38-$0C3F, are not referenced (the timer loop at $131C stops at $0C37).
First entry of the point list of the tile face being drawn (up to five corner numbers at $0C40-$0C44), written by the tile-shape code at $2D54/$2D76 and read through the pointer at $3C.
Second corner number of the tile face being drawn ($2D5C/$2D7E).
Third corner number of the tile face being drawn ($2D65/$2D84).
Fourth corner number of the tile face being drawn ($2D57/$2D89).
Fifth entry of the tile face's point list, written only at $2D79. $0C45-$0C46 after it are not referenced.
Bit 7 tells the object drawer which of the two passes it is on for objects drawn in two phases ($8548, flipped $8582, $85B1).
Leftmost tile found for the previous landscape row, reused as the starting guess for the next row ($26CD, $26DB).
Tile column where the next big 3D digit of the secret code is built on the landscape ($3213, $323D-$3275).
Tile row of the 3D digit being built ($3217, $3228).
Bit 7 set while the title picture is drawn ($3295 ROR, $32C1 LSR); tested by the tile drawer at $2A1F.

How the view's background is filled: $2211 takes two alternating fill bytes from $2286+kind and $228A+kind: 0 = $00/$55 stripes (the sky in play), 1 = plain $00, 2 = $AA/$55, 3 = plain $55, to which $1090 adds stars. Set by the title and preview code ($13AE, $140F), hyperspace ($2175) and the game-over picture ($87E2); read $10A4, $2226.

Bit 7: redraw an object without the landscape behind it ($1FEF). Cleared at $1F98, set with $C0 by the game-over picture ($87EB). A C64 addition reads it in the play interrupt: while bit 7 is set it plots random dots over the view, 4 per band ($9623) and 12 per frame once the landscape is over ($9690, when $0C4E bit 7 is set), the game-over decay.

Bit 7 set when the landscape has ended: $1A00-$1A02 store $80 when the player's energy runs out, and $35E2-$35E7 copy $0CDE into it when a hyperspace ended the game. The gameplay loop shows the game-over picture when it is non-zero ($12A2); also tested by the object redraw ($204C, $2059), $3588 and the play interrupt ($9645).
$40 when an enemy scanning the player can see the robot but not its square ($1952); the C64 scanner at $168F then leaves the lower half of the scanner empty.
Divides the enemy timer updates: $1317 only counts the timers when it is 0 and then reloads it with 2, otherwise $1331 decrements it, so the timers move on every third call.

Bit 6 set means a U key press may start a U-turn: set to $40 by $11EA-$11EC whenever no pan or action key is down, cleared at $1281; the action code shifts it out at $1B2F so holding U turns only once; $35B5 reads it.

Zero for landscape 0000, non-zero otherwise (the high BCD byte, or the low one when the high is 0): set by $33F9/$3400. Landscape 0000 skips the code question ($104D) and is handled specially at $1420, $145C and $2AD7.
Low byte of the angle in radians inside $0E75 ($0E7E), turned into its complement at $0F06-$0F09 for the second pass; read $0EAE, $0ECE.
High byte of the radians value in $0E75 ($0E83, complemented $0F0E-$0F11; read $0EB6, $0ED5).

Offset of the landscape's secret-code stash on page $3F. Only reached through disguised indexed operands: written by $2A5A (STA $0C4D,X with X=8, from $0C7D by $2A57), read by $14AC (LDY $0BAB,X with X=$AA) for the loop whose STA $3F00,Y at $14C7 fills the stash, and by $254F (LDA $0B56,X with X=$FF), which adds 41 for the stash pointer in $0C/$0D. In work/play-l0000.vsf it is $8D and the 43 stash bytes sit at $3F8D-$3FB7, over the tail of the start-up code at $3F00.
Bit 7 set when the square being tested by $1DF9 holds the target object ($1E13); tested $1E90, cleared $1CDF, rotated $18F9.
High byte of the yaw of the object being measured, relative to the viewer ($8425); read $170E/$172A, $18BE, $20C6/$20E6, $84ED.
Object number an enemy is draining or aiming at: stored $188C, $1AEA; read $191A, $1A08, compared by the gaze code at $1E0E.
Low byte of the object's yaw relative to the viewer ($841A); read $20BE/$20DE, $84E5. The next byte, $0C5A, is not referenced.
Low byte of the object's height relative to the viewer, the opposite side of the viewer-object triangle ($846C); read $850A, $8561.
High byte of the relative height ($8471); read $8511, $855C.
Low byte of the object's horizontal distance from the viewer, the adjacent side ($8462); read $84AB.
High byte of the horizontal distance ($8467); read $84B3.

Bit 7 set while the sights are shown: toggled by SPACE at $11BA-$11BF, cleared at $359B and $87D7. With it set the pan keys move the sights ($11F1), action keys below $22 are allowed ($12D9), and the C64 scroller moves sprite 0 along with the view ($96D0, $9716).
Bit 7 set: digits are printed as big 3D blocks on the landscape ($31FC); set at $33B9 for the secret code, cleared $33DD.

Logger value of the action key being carried out, stored at $12DE: $1B1B treats $22 as hyperspace, $1B2B $23 as the U-turn, and $1B4E tests bit 5. $211D also stores here the type of an object about to be made, which $2131 copies into the type table at $0A40, so the create keys' logger values serve as object types.
Column offset of the left edge of the object being redrawn, relative to the screen's left edge ($20D8, $20FA; $1FC4-$2012).

Bit 7 set when the player moved to another square or turned round: set to $80 at $1B87-$1B89 (transfer and U-turn) and at $21A9 (hyperspace); the gameplay loop shifts it out at $12B1/$1302 and returns.
Bit 7 set when F1 was pressed ($11AB); the gameplay loop ($12B6) and $3580 then end the game.

Result bits of the secret-code comparison in $1450: each pass of the loop at $14BA-$14C0 rotates in whether a generated BCD byte equals the byte at $0C6F+X; X runs down from $AA (or $A5) to $80, so only the last comparisons meet the entered code at $0CF0-$0CF3 and the rest compare against bytes up to $0D19. Read at $14DC. $0C66 after it is not referenced.
Bit 7 set when the square tested by $1DF9 holds a boulder ($1E57); cleared $1D05, read $1D29.
Width of the viewing arc of the enemy being handled ($16F4, $1988); compared at $18C7.
Width in columns of the buffer used to redraw an object, at most 20 ($210B, clamped at $2105-$2109); read $1FE2-$2021.
Width in columns of the visible part of the object being redrawn ($20FD, $201E); read $2015.
Counter over the objects in a stack while it is drawn ($21C1, $21EA, $21EF, $220B).
Object number at the top of the stack being drawn ($21B0; read $21E7, $21FF).

How a changed object is put on screen by $1F9F: bit 6 dissolve it in ($2047), bit 7 take the sights off first (on the C64 by turning sprite 0 off, $1FA9-$1FB2). $C0 at $12F3 after an action and $87EE; 0 at $1F95; also $1878; read $1FA9, $2047.

Bit 7 set while an enemy checks whether it can see a robot, so the gaze test also reports a robot it sees without seeing its square ($18DD, $1904, $1B40; read $1D26). $322F reads $0C6E+7 = $0C75 with X=7, not this byte.

Number of enemies on this landscape, Sentinel included (1-8): $1434; read $143A, $1515/$158A; the tree count starts from 48 minus three per enemy ($147D-$1489). $14BA reads $0C6F+X with X from $AA down to $80, a secret-code loop, not this byte.
Sound counter for one note of a chord in the music player ($34F5, $34FE).
Bit 7 set: build the landscape and its code without previewing or playing it; set to $80 at $219D on the hyperspace path, tested $14AF and $2C19, shifted out $14CE.
Bit 7 set while the game is paused ($34C3 ROR, $34DA LSR); the play interrupt then only scans the pause keys ($964A).

What the sound code is doing: 3 music ($8892-$8894), 6 the game-over sound ($35EA-$35EC, $87C4-$87C6); the drain code stores the scanner sound's value from Y at $195F after comparing it at $195B; read at $1955 and $3531.
Falling pitch of the game-over sound: $E6 at $87CB, decremented at $355A, read $3540.
Anti-tamper value made at $18B5 from the hidden landscape byte at $0F3D; $322D-$3232 read it (as $0C6E,X with X=7) and compare it with $0F3D. $2A57 reads $0C75+8 = $0C7D, not this byte.
Set by the enemy gaze code when a tree is in the way: bit 7 for the target's square, bit 6 for the robot itself ($1901); read $17B7. $0C77 after it is not referenced.
Horizontal offset added while drawing the title and preview pictures ($13F0, $140C), 0 in play; subtracted at $285E and $85D0. $0C79 is not referenced.
Bit 7 set: polygon edges are drawn in the fill colour ($22E2); set and cleared by the object drawer ($853A, $85BE).

Five-byte shift register $0C7B-$0C7F that generates the landscape's seed numbers ($31CA shifts eight bits per call and returns $0C7F). $0C7B takes the low BCD byte of the landscape number at $33F0; the start-up code fills all five with 1 at $3F96-$3F9E.
Second byte of the seed register: the high BCD byte of the landscape number at $33ED; cleared with $0C7D-$0C7F at $360F.
Third byte of the seed register: set to 1 by $1193 after the reset, feeds the register's feedback ($31CF), copied to $0C55 at $2A57.
Fourth byte of the seed register ($31E2).
Top byte of the seed register: the value each $31CA call returns ($31EE) and part of the feedback ($31D5).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: which object the enemy's search for a tree to turn into a meanie has reached ($1982, $1991, $19A1, $19FA).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: energy the enemy has drained and still has to spend by planting trees ($1A52/$1A58 add, $1A60/$1A7A spend).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: the target for which the enemy found no tree to turn into a meanie, so it does not search again ($1978, $199C; compared $17D2).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: failed meanie searches ($197D, $1996; read $1859).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: bit 7 clear when the enemy has made a meanie, with its object number in bits 0-6 ($19EB, $1768, $1975; read $16F7-$1873, $1BFF/$1C06).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: object number of the enemy's current target ($1826; read $1701, $179A, $1935, $1999, $19B1).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: bit 7 set when the enemy sees the target's square, bit 6 when it sees only the robot ($182B; read $1943).
Eight bytes, one per enemy: bit 7 set to make the enemy look for something to drain on its next turn ($1862, $1792; read $177F). The byte after, $0CC0, is not referenced.

Scroll steps still to do in the current pan: loaded from $0CD1 at $3663; the play interrupt raises $0CD8 while it is non-zero ($964F-$9656); each step at $96A6 decrements it ($972A); $368F waits for 0.
Address of the top-left of the view's image in the bitmap-layout area, $E140 on the C64 (set $1339/$133E); the star plotter adds it at $9415/$941D.
High byte of the view image address, $E1 ($133E, read $941D). $0CC4-$0CC5 after it are not referenced on the C64, whose sights are a sprite.

Horizontal position of the sights in view pixels, $10-$8F: $50 when shown ($1354), moved by one per step at $996C-$9990; pushing past either edge wraps it by 64 and starts a pan. Copied to $9B for sprite 0; read by $1C10 to aim.
Vertical position of the sights, $20-$9F: $5F when shown ($135D), moved at $99A2-$99D2 (stops at the edge when the view is at a pitch limit); copied to $9C; read by $1C2D.
Bit pattern that makes the sights start moving slowly: $6B at $11E2 while no pan key is down, shifted left at $11F6 on each move call, and the sights only move when a 0 comes out.

Written as 0 at $3598 and $87D4 but not read by any traced C64 code: the BBC kept the count of screen bytes saved under its drawn sights here; the C64 sights are a sprite. $0CCA-$0CCD after it are not referenced either.
Bit 7 set: skip the stash test hidden in the visibility code ($254A); bit 7 is set at $2573.
Mask with the same number of leading zero bits as the buffer width minus 1, from the table at $15C4 ($86B6-$86B9); limits the random column at $86F8.
Random byte for one dissolve step ($86F2), supplying the line pair ($8706), the row ($870F) and the pixel mask index ($876F).
Number of scroll steps for the pan just drawn: cleared at $364B, set by $9929 (16 sideways, 8 up or down); copied to $0CC1 at $3660.
Bytes left in one batch of the dissolve: 96 at $86BC-$86BE, counted down at $879C; after each batch the sound code runs ($87A1).
Width in columns of the buffer being dissolved in, copied at $86A5-$86A8 from $211B; the random column is wrapped by it ($86FB-$8700). The BBC used the width in bytes.
Minimum on-screen width used when working out how much of an object to redraw ($19F5, $1A46; read $20AC-$20B8). $0CD5-$0CD6 are not referenced.
Bit 7 set: do not show the sights ($2063 ROR, $2085 LSR); the C64 sprite routine $99DC neither positions nor enables sprite 0 while it is set.

C64 addition. Bit 7 is set by the play interrupt ($9654-$9656) whenever scroll steps are left in $0CC1; the pan loop at $3668 waits for it, does one step ($96A6 and the missing $B006) and clears it at $368C. While it is set the interrupt leaves the enemy timers and scanner to the pan loop ($965E). $0CD9-$0CDB are not referenced.
Copy of $0CE4 from the last key poll ($121F); the gameplay loop reads it at $1291 to see whether a pan key was being acted on.
Bit 7 set when the gaze being traced has met a tree ($1E96 ROR; $1CE2 LSR; $18FE ROL).
Bit 7 set when a hyperspace ended the landscape, bit 6 when it won it ($217A, $2198); read $245B, $35A8, $35E2.

Frames left of the current sound: set by the sound and music code ($34AD, $3501, $3557, $3563, $3622), counted down once a frame by the play interrupt ($9630, held at 0 by $9635). $0CE0-$0CE3 after it are not referenced.

Bit 7 set while a key action (pan, absorb, create...) is being carried out: set by $1214, cleared at $127E; the play interrupt stops polling keys while it is set ($9669) and $347D skips the volume keys.

Bit 7 set until the player first acts: the gameplay loop clears it at $12E1 when an action key is used; while set the play interrupt does not run the enemy timers or scanner ($9659) and $367F skips them in the pan loop.
6 when the player stands on the Sentinel's tower, anything else otherwise ($1B7F); used when the next secret code is made ($33C4-$33D7), where a wrong value spoils the code.
Position in the music being played, bit 7 set when none plays ($888F, $34DE-$3518; read $35D8, $362D).
Key logger entry 0: the sideways pan key (0 right, 1 left), bit 7 set for none. Filled by $1363 ($1367, $1380), read at $1201, $122C, $9965; the pause code sets it to $80 ($9687).
Key logger entry 1: the action key (absorb, transfer, create, hyperspace, U-turn) as its logger value, bit 7 set for none; read at $11E5 and $12D0.
Key logger entry 2: the vertical pan key (2 up, 3 down), bit 7 for none; read $1206, $1231, $1389, $9999.
Key logger entry 3: the pause and volume keys, read by $3485 and $34BA/$34CE. $0CEC-$0CEF after it are set to $80 by the reset but not otherwise referenced.

Eight-byte keyboard buffer for the landscape number and code, newest character at the low end ($32DE-$332F). $3357 packs it into BCD pairs, lowest pair first, at $0CF0-$0CF3; $1044-$1047 hand the landscape number to $33ED and $1057 puts landscape 0000's code here. Characters from $0CF4 are overwritten with $FF as they are packed ($337C-$337E).
Input buffer bytes 1-6 ($0CF1-$0CF6): $0CF1 gives the high BCD byte of the entered landscape number at $1044, and $32FF/$3328 move the buffer up a byte per key typed.
Last byte of the input buffer: $330A-$330C put a space here when the buffer contents move up. $0CF8-$0CFB after it are not referenced ($2A $AA $A2 $00 in the image).
Bit 7 set while no landscape is being played (title, preview): set by $114E and at start-up ($3F04); the play interrupt ($9640) only runs the game's timers and key polls when it is clear.
Low BCD byte of the landscape number 0000-9999, set at $33F6; read $1A8C, $33E7, $35FA. The hand-over image holds $03 here and $00 at $0CFE: whoever froze the game had entered landscape 0003.
High BCD byte of the landscape number ($33F3); read $1A90, $33E1, $3426, $35F7. The byte after it, $0CFF, is not referenced.

An RTI and two zero bytes that nothing reaches: no traced instruction jumps or points a vector here, and the C64's NMI vector is set to $8F98 ($890B/$8910). In the BBC original the operating system sent NMIs to this address and the two bytes after it held a saved interrupt vector; the C64 build kept the RTI and left the two bytes zero.

Unsigned 8-bit multiply: A * $75, 16-bit result with the high byte in A and the low byte in $74. Shift-and-add unrolled eight times; X and Y untouched. Called by the sine/cosine code ($0EA3, $0EA6, $0F51), the 16x16 multiply ($0FC7-$0FEF), the gaze code ($1DD4), smoothing ($2B5B) and the object angle code ($849B, $84D0). Byte for byte the BBC routine.
Second entry into the multiply at $0D03 that skips its first STA: multiplies the value already in $74 by $75 (high byte in A, low in $74). Used only by $0F4A.

Arctangent of a ratio: given a smaller unsigned 16-bit value in A (high) and $74 (low) and a larger one in $76/$77, divides them by shift-and-subtract to get the tangent times 256 in $7E, looks the angle up in the tables read as $3B00,Y (low bytes) and $3C01,Y (high bytes) (interpolating with two extra quotient bits kept in $78) and returns it in $8A/$8B, 16 bits to a full turn, so 0 to $2000 (45 degrees). A quotient that overflows (a ratio of 1) leaves through $0E03 with $7E = $FF and the angle $2000. Called from $92DB and $9319. Same bytes as the BBC routine.

Sine and cosine of a 16-bit angle (A high, $74 low) to about 15 bits: reduces the angle into one quadrant as radians ($0F3E), evaluates a short polynomial with the multiplies at $0D03/$0F4A (small-angle form, or the complementary angle past $7A), and does it twice ($60 counts the passes) so that X=0 fills sine and X=1 cosine. Stores magnitudes in $0C02/$0C00 (sine) and $0C03/$0C01 (cosine), then sets bit 0 of a low byte when that value is negative (sine for angles past 180 degrees at $0F19, cosine in the second and third quadrants at $0F26). Keeps X in $0F3B. Called from $1C54 and $1C6F when turning the sights direction into a vector. Unchanged from the BBC code; $0E9A-$0EA0 can never run, since both branches before it jump.

Not a variable, a decoy base address: $2C5F stores to $0F1D+X with X=$20, which reaches $0F3D, the hidden landscape byte (see $0F3C). The bytes from here to $0F35 are the sign fix-ups at the end of $0E75: bit 0 of $0C00 set for a negative sine ($0F19-$0F23), bit 0 of $0C01 for a negative cosine ($0F26-$0F34).

Not a variable, a decoy base address: $18A4 (LDA) and $3232 (CMP) use $0F36+X with X=7, which reaches $0F3D, the hidden landscape byte. The bytes $0F36-$0F3A are the last byte of the STA $0C01 at $0F34 and the X restore and RTS that end $0E75.
One byte where $0E75 keeps X: stored at $0E78, reloaded at $0F37.

An LDA #imm that is never executed: its operand byte, $0F3D, is where the game hides a copy of the landscape number's high BCD byte for its anti-tamper checks. $2C5C-$2C5F copy it from $AD4E (with X=$20, disguised as STA $0F1D,X); $AD4E is the third of the 81 seed numbers stored by $2ACC, which is still the high byte fed into the seed register at $33ED. $18A2-$18A4 read it back as LDA $0F36,X with X=7 to build $0C75, and $322D-$3232 compare $0C75 with it (CMP $0F36,X, X=7). Same arrangement as the BBC original.

Turns the 16-bit angle in A (high) and $74 (low) into radians within its quadrant: drops the top two bits (the quadrant) by shifting left twice, then multiplies by $C9 through $0F4A, so a right angle gives about $C900 (1 radian = $8000). Result high byte in $75, low byte in A and $74. Only caller: $0E7B.

Multiplies the 16-bit value $76 (high) / $74 (low) by the 8-bit $75 and keeps the top 16 bits of the 24-bit product: high byte in $75, low byte in A and $74. Built from two 8x8 multiplies ($0D05, $0D03). Called by $0EAB, $0EDC and the hypotenuse routine at $9395; $0F3E falls into it.

Tests one key: X is the C64 key number (bits 0-2 the keyboard row driven on $DC00, bits 3-5 the column bit read from $DC01; $20 is F1, $27 SPACE). Calls $FFF4 with A=$81 and Y=$FF, the BBC's scan-one-key request, which the C64 layer passes to $8CF9; it answers X=$FF when the key is down. Returns Z set if down; Y is preserved. Same bytes as the BBC routine, only the key numbers passed by its callers ($11A5, $11B0, $1370) are C64 ones.

8-bit sine and cosine of an angle in A (256 to a turn; bit 7 of $74 adds half a step): folds the angle into a quadrant, reads the 128-entry sine table at $AC80 at the angle and at its complement, and stores |sin| in $8E and |cos| in $8F, swapping them as the quadrant needs. Leaves the angle in $67 so that bit 7 is the sine's sign and bit 6 the cosine's. Only caller $848F (object point angles). The BBC routine read its table at $5980; the C64 copy reads $AC80, $5300 higher, as the moved data block requires.

Signed 16x16 multiply keeping the top 16 bits: ($6B,$6A) is two's complement, ($69,$68) sign-magnitude with the sign in bit 0 of $68, and bit 7 of $67 is an extra sign. Makes both positive (flipping bit 7 of $67 for each negative), adds the three significant partial products from $0D03 (the low-by-low one is replaced by a rounding constant $80) and returns the result in A (high) and $74 (low) with the sign applied by falling into $1007. Only caller $1C93.

If the N flag is clear on entry, returns (A high, $74 low) unchanged; if it is set, falls into $1009 and negates it. Callers load or BIT-test a high byte just before, so this gives an absolute value ($1DD8, $2B5F, $3019, $3040) or applies a sign (the end of $0F9E).
Negates the 16-bit value with its high byte in A and low byte in $74: returns the new high byte in A (the old one is left in $75) and the low byte in $74. Called by $0E46, $1CB5, $84A6, $8502.

Start of the title sequence, entered from the start-up code ($3FB1) and jumped to from $3585 and $363A. Resets the stack to $01FF, sets all four colours to blue (A=6 to $8643: the BBC code passed 4, which is blue in the BBC palette, 6 is blue on the C64), resets the game state ($114D), draws the title picture ($3282 with A=0), prints token 0 (PRESS ANY KEY) through $8617, selects the title colours (A=$87) and waits for a key ($8629). Then falls into $1034.

Asks for a landscape: resets state ($114D), prints token 1 (LANDSCAPE NUMBER?), reads four digits ($32D5 with A=4), packs them into BCD ($3357) and seeds the landscape generator with them ($33ED, X = low byte from $0CF0, Y = high byte from $0CF1). For landscape 0000 ($0C52 = 0) it copies the stored code at $108C into $0CF0-$0CF3 and skips the question; otherwise it prints token 2 (SECRET ENTRY CODE?) and reads eight digits. Reached from $1017 and from $1089.

Blanks the screen to blue (A=6 to $8643) and calls the landscape builder $2ACC; also entered from $3600 to replay a landscape without asking for the code again. The stack was reset at $1017, so the JSR at $1071 leaves its return address in $01FE/$01FF; when the entered code is right, $2C1E-$2C26 overwrite it with $8816 and the builder's RTS continues at $8817 (the landscape preview) instead of here. A normal return means the code was wrong and falls into $1074.

Wrong secret code: reached by falling out of $1071 and by the JMP at $886F when the preview's own check of the code (in $1450) fails. Resets state, redraws the title ($3282 with A=0), selects the title colours (A=$87), prints token 3 (WRONG SECRET CODE and PRESS ANY KEY), waits for a key ($8629) and goes back to $1034.

Four BCD bytes $87 $53 $04 $06, the eight-digit secret code of landscape 0000 (06045387) stored low byte first like the input buffer. $1052-$105B copy them to $0CF0-$0CF3 so that landscape 0000 never asks for a code while the generator's checks still find the right one.

Clears the play screen before a view is drawn: $1336 resets the view's screen origin and the screen matrix, $8607 fills the 320 bytes above the view image ($E000-$E13F, the row of energy icons and scanner) with $55, $2993 (A=0) and $2211 (A=0, Y=24 rows, X=40 columns) fill the view with the background kind in $0C4C, and when that kind is 3 (black sky) $93F5 draws 40 stars, three times over. The same sequence as the BBC routine with the C64's own targets. Called from $13E4, $35AF, $35C0.

Draws the strip of landscape a pan needs and starts the scroll. Direction in $08: 0 right, 1 left, 2 up, 3 down. Turns the viewer by the step at $9925+Y (yaw +20/-8, pitch +4/-12), fills the off-screen column buffer ($3912) or row buffer ($38AD) with alternate $55 and $00 bytes, the striped sky (the BBC called its general fill routine here), selects that buffer ($994F or $9939) and draws the view ($2625). If drawing was abandoned because the pan key was let go (carry set) the turn is undone ($10F4, $113E); otherwise the angle is settled to the net step (8 yaw units sideways, 4 pitch units up or down) and $9929 sets 16 or 8 scroll steps. An up or down pan does nothing when the pitch already equals the limit at $114B or $114C. Called from $365A.
Not a variable: the two operand bytes of the JMP $113A at $1148. The pitch-limit test at $1102 reads $1149+Y with Y = 2 (up) or 3 (down), which lands on $114B and $114C.

$35 (+53): the highest pitch the player's view may reach. $1102 refuses an up pan when the viewer's pitch equals it, and the C64 sights code at $99AE stops the sights at the top edge instead of starting a pan. The test is an exact match: it works because every object starts at pitch $F5 ($1F7E) and pans move it in steps of 4, so the pitch meets $35 exactly.
$CD (-51): the lowest pitch the player's view may reach, tested by the same exact match at $1102 (Y=3) and by the sights code at $99C8.

Resets the game state before the title or a landscape: sets bit 7 of $0CFC (no game running), then in one loop clears the object tables $0900-$09EF and $0A00-$0AEF, zero page $02-$B1, $0100-$01BF (object flags, pitches, tile visibility) and $0C00-$0CE3, and sets $0CE4-$0CEF to $80. The C64 version skips $00/$01, the processor port, and clears up to $B1 because its own variables go up to there; the BBC cleared $00-$8F. LDX #0 appears twice ($1151, $1153). Falls into $117C. Called from $101F, $1034, $1074, $35F4.

C64 addition first: switches the display to the title's bitmap screen in bank 3 (A=0 to $9A51). Then the BBC routine from $1181: marks every square visible ($3E80-$3EFF = $FF), frees all 64 object slots ($0100-$013F = $80), steps the seed byte $0C7D, restores the column-buffer pitch limits ($9954); and a second C64 addition turns all sprites off ($D015 = 0). Reached from $114D and called from $3615.

Reads the game keys once a frame, called from the play interrupt ($9678) while $0CE4 bit 7 is clear and the delay in $130B has run out. Sets $09 to $80 (no pan); F1 sets bit 7 of $0C64 (quit); SPACE toggles the sights ($0C5F) once per press ($1236), showing them through $134C and $99DC (the C64 sights are sprite 0) or hiding them through $9A3C. Then scans the logged keys ($1363, Y=$0E). No pan key: resets the sights' start-up pacing ($0CC8 = $6B), passes an action key to $1214, or re-arms the U-turn ($0C51 = $40). A pan key: moves the sights ($9958, paced by $0CC8) when they are shown, otherwise puts the direction in $09 and $0C1D. Ends by copying $0CE4 to $0CDC ($121C).

Sets bit 7 of $0CE4 and $0C1E so that the game concentrates on the key action just started (the play interrupt stops reading keys while $0CE4 bit 7 is set, $9669), then at $121C copies $0CE4 into $0CDC and returns. Called from $12AC, $1B69, $21A0 and reached from $119F.

With interrupts off, rescans the pan keys ($1363, Y=3) and compares the key logger's sideways ($0CE8) and vertical ($0CEA) entries with the last pan direction in $0C1D. Z set if the same pan key is still down. Used by $1296 and by the view drawer at $2765, which gives up a pan strip once the key is released.

SPACE latch for the sights toggle: $11D0-$11D6 store $80 while SPACE is down and 0 once it is up, and $11B5 only toggles the sights when this is 0, so holding SPACE toggles once. The following byte, $1237, is not referenced by any traced instruction.

Tries to put object X on a random empty, flat square whose height is below A: picks a column and a row with $1272, points at the square ($2BA8) and accepts it if it holds no object (byte below $C0), is flat (low nibble 0) and is lower than the limit (high nibble); $1F16 then places the object. After every 256 misses the limit rises by one; when it reaches 12 the routine gives up. Carry clear on success, set on failure. The BBC's call to $2BA8's counterpart returned the square byte and the object test in the flags; the C64 version loads and tests the square here ($1257-$125B). Called from $1478, $14A1, $1A6D, $2165.
Next number from the landscape's seed sequence ($31CA) reduced to 0-30: keeps the low five bits and draws again when they are 31. Picks random tile coordinates for $1238.

The loop that runs while the player stands still. Clears $0CE4 and $0C51 and, a C64 addition, sets $130B to 2 so that the interrupt's next key scan waits a frame. Each pass without a pending key action notes whether the same pan key is still held ($0C1F via $1223), runs the enemies ($16B5), shows the game-over picture if the landscape is over ($0C4E, $87B1 with A=$1E), returns carry set when the player moved or turned ($0C63) or pressed F1 ($0C64), and otherwise updates the energy drain ($191F), the pause keys ($34BA), sound ($352C) and the volume keys ($347D). With a key pending: returns carry clear for a pan ($09); for an action key ($0CE9; codes below $22 need the sights on) stores it in $0C61, wakes the enemies (bit 7 of $0CE5 cleared), silences sound channel 0 ($3525) and runs the action ($1B18); on success plays sound 2 ($3470), redraws the changed object ($1F9F) and the energy icons ($9508). The C64 silences channel 0 before trying the action; the BBC did it after a success. Called from $363D.

C64 addition; the BBC has no byte here (its timer routine follows the gameplay loop directly). Frames to wait before the raster interrupt resumes its key-press check: the gameplay loop start stores 2 ($1284-$1286); the interrupt ($966E-$9678) decrements it while it is non-zero and calls the key checker at $119F only once it reads 0, so after each (re)start of the loop one frame passes without a key check, then it runs every frame. 0 in both snapshots.

C64 addition in front of the BBC's enemy timer routine. Adds $CD to the phase byte at $1335 and returns unless the addition carries, so the tick at $1317 runs on 205 of every 256 calls. Called by the raster interrupt at most once a frame ($9663, reached only with bit 7 of $0CFC, $0C4E, $0C72, $0CE5 and $0CD8 all clear, so not while paused) and, when a pan is being scrolled, by the main loop after each scroll step instead ($3684, skipped while $0CE5 bit 7 is set). With the tick's own one-in-three divider the timers at $0C20-$0C37 count about 13.4 times a second on a PAL machine when called every frame (50.1 frames a second x 205/256 / 3), where the BBC's interrupt, on a 20 ms timer, made it 16.7. Why the C64 slows the enemies down is not known.

The BBC's enemy timer tick, byte for byte, reached here only by falling through from the gate at $130C. While the divider $0C50 is non-zero it is decremented and nothing else happens; when it is 0 it is reset to 2 and each of the 24 timers at $0C20-$0C37 that holds 2 or more is decremented, so a timer counts down to 1 and stays there. Three timers per enemy n (0-7): $0C20+n drain, $0C28+n turn, $0C30+n tactics.

C64 addition: the running fraction for the gate at $130C, advanced by $CD on every call ($130C-$1312, its only reader and writer); a carry out of it lets the enemy timer tick run. 0 in both snapshots.

C64 rewrite of the BBC's screen-start reset, called first by the screen clear at $1090. With interrupts off: sets the drawing base $0CC2/$0CC3 to $E140, one character row (320 bytes) into the bank-3 bitmap at $E000 (the random-dot plotter at $93FB adds its offsets to it, wraps past $FFFF back to $E000 and skips $FF40-$FFFF); zeroes the pan offsets $94 (columns, 0-39) and $95 (rows, 0-24) that $96A6 steps; and calls $9AAC to lay out the screen matrix at $7C00 again. The BBC set its base to $60C0, fetched its icon-row address and wrote the 6845 start-address registers, which have no C64 counterpart.

C64 rewrite of the BBC's sights set-up. Clears sprite 0's X bit 8 in $D010 ($134C-$1351) and puts the sights in the middle of the view: $0CC6 = 80 (x, 0-159) and $0CC7 = 95 (y), copied to $9B/$9C, from which $99DC positions sprite 0, the crosshair whose shape is at $7000. The BBC instead worked out where in its bitmap to draw the sights ($0CC4/$0CC5), which the C64 never reads or writes. Called when SPACE turns the sights on ($11C4) and by the play-screen set-up ($98C7).

Fills the four-entry key log $0CE8-$0CEB. Marks every entry empty ($80), then for Y down to 0 tests the key whose matrix code is at $138D+Y (through $0F62, the C64's OSBYTE $81 at $8F78 and the matrix test at $8CF9) and, when it is held, stores (slot byte >> 2) into entry (slot byte AND 3), the slot byte being $139C+Y; a key tested later (lower Y) overwrites one tested earlier in the same entry. Returns A = $0CE8 AND $0CEA, so N is clear when a pan key (S, D, L, comma) is held. Y picks how far the scan starts: 14 from the key checker ($11D9), 3 for the pan keys alone ($1224), 13 from the interrupt while paused ($967E, which then empties entries 0-2). The code is the BBC's; only the key table differs.

The 15 game keys as C64 keyboard-matrix codes (column x 8 + row, the form the key test at $8CF9 takes), in the order scan_game_keys reads them: $29 S, $12 D, $15 L, $3D comma, $11 A, $37 Q, $0A R, $32 T, $23 B, $2B H, $03 7, $1B 8, $10 CRSR-right, $38 CRSR-down, $33 U. The BBC table held its negative INKEY numbers for the same letters, with COPY and DELETE where the C64 uses CRSR-right (pause) and CRSR-down (resume).

Where scan_game_keys files each key of $138D: bits 0-1 pick the log entry $0CE8+n, bits 2-7 are the value stored there. Entry 0 sideways pan (S 1, D 0); entry 2 vertical pan (L 2, comma 3); entry 1 actions (A 32 absorb, Q 33 transfer, R 0, T 2, B 3 = the type to create, H 34 hyperspace, U 35 U-turn); entry 3 volume and pause (7 0 quieter, 8 1 louder, CRSR-right 2 pause, CRSR-down 3 resume; used at $3485 and $34BA). The same 15 bytes as the BBC's table.

Draws one of the pictures made with the 3D engine. A = object to stand on a tower at the right (5 Sentinel for the title, $32BA; 0 robot for the secret-code screen, $32A7; $80 none for the landscape preview, $885F), kept in $0C1C; X = background kind for the clear at $1090, kept in $0C4C (1 plain, 3 stars); Y = view, kept in $141F (1 title screens, 0 preview). Patches the drop-shadow text colours in the VDU sequence at $AA96 (front X EOR 3 at $AA97, shadow 2 or 3 at $AAA2), sets viewer object 16 from the tables at $1413-$141D ($0950 height, $0150 pitch, $0910 x, $0990 z, $09D0 yaw), clears the screen ($1090), draws the object ($887E) unless A has bit 7 set, sets the 3D-text x offset $0C78 from $1419+Y and draws the view from object 16 ($2625). After a preview it zeroes the 128-byte tile visibility table at $3E80 and sets $141F to $7F. Leaves $0C78 and $0C4C at 0. The BBC routine with its addresses moved.
Height of the viewer (object 16) for draw_title_view, copied to $0950: 33 for the landscape preview (Y = 0), 75 for the title and secret-code screens (Y = 1).
Pitch of the title viewer, copied to $0150: $EA (-22) for the preview, $D9 (-39) for the title screens.
x position of the title viewer, copied to $0910: 15 for the preview, 0 for the title screens.
Offset for the large 3D title text, put in $0C78 while draw_title_view draws: 0 for the preview, $EF (-17) for the title screens.
z position of the title viewer, copied to $0990: $C2 (194) for the preview, $BF (191) for the title screens.
Yaw of the title viewer, copied to $09D0: 0 for the preview, 18 for the title screens. All six viewer tables at $1413-$141E hold the BBC's values.

Which picture draw_title_view is making (Y: 0 preview, 1 title screens), stored at $13BF; after a preview $1401 sets it to $7F, and it stays non-zero from then on (1 at the hand-over, $7F in play). The object-angle routine reads it at $843B to tell the preview from everything else.

Decides how many enemies a landscape has and places them. Landscape 0000 ($0C52 = 0, set by $33F9) gets one; any other gets the count from $3426, capped at $0C07.
